summary: This project aims to advance retinal ganglion cell (RGC) transplant therapy for glaucoma by developing nanoparticle-based optical coherence tomography (OCT) contrast agents to track transplanted cells in vivo with high spatial resolution. The proposed method uses gold nanorods (GNRs) to maximize contrast between donor RGCs and the retina in OCT imaging, and investigates the correlation between GNR signals and RGC fate in vitro and in vivo. The study will also examine the effects of cell number and injection location on transplant success rate and leverage advanced imaging to optimize RGC transplantation.
